title: Where There Is Will, but Not a Way: Two Coaches’ Perspectives From a Collaborative 5Cs Psychological Skills Training Intervention in a Major League Soccer Development Academy
abstract: Coaches are central agents in athletes’ psychosocial development, yet few receive structured preparation for psychological skills training. This study explored the perspectives of two professional Major League Soccer Academy coaches regarding a co-produced, 4-week psychological skills training intervention grounded in Harwood’s 5Cs. It is guided by a relational-constructivist paradigm and informed by principles of cultural praxis. Semistructured interviews were conducted 2 weeks before, 1 month after, and 18 months postintervention, supported by observations and reflexive field notes. Reflexive thematic analysis revealed an overarching theme: where there is will, but not a way . The coaches reported enhanced psychosocial efficacy, with the 5Cs providing structure and language that meaningfully informed daily practice. However, organizational volatility, driven by staff turnover and entrenched performance pressures, created an implementation-sustainability gap that individual coach motivation could not bridge. Findings highlight that sustained psychological skills training integration requires institutional embedding, leadership commitment, and culturally informed collaboration, conditions that remain precarious in professional football.
